classification.difficultyReason: Read each labelled angle from south, identify east or west, and subtract from or add to 180 degrees to express the clockwise bearing from north.

content.prompt: Express the bearings shown in each diagram as a compass bearing and a true bearing.

spec.description: Dashed compass axes, north arrow, central point and southeast ray to P; the arc is 60 degrees east of south.
spec.mathematics: P has offset proportional to (sin120, cos120); the supplied angle is between south and OP.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied 60-degree angle is labelled.

answer.worked:
The direction is $60^\circ$ east of south, so the compass bearing is $\mathrm{S}60^\circ\mathrm{E}$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{True bearing}&=180^\circ-60^\circ\\\text{True bearing}&=120^\circ\mathrm{T}.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Dashed compass axes, north arrow, central point and southwest ray to P; the arc is 30 degrees west of south.
spec.mathematics: P has offset proportional to (sin210, cos210); the supplied angle is between OP and south.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied 30-degree angle is labelled.

answer.worked:
The direction is $30^\circ$ west of south, so the compass bearing is $\mathrm{S}30^\circ\mathrm{W}$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{True bearing}&=180^\circ+30^\circ\\\text{True bearing}&=210^\circ\mathrm{T}.\end{align*}$$
